# Findings

*Generated by `src/findings.mjs` on every build. Every number here is computed from
`data/models.json` — nothing in this file is written by hand, so it cannot drift from
the data. A catalogue refresh can rewrite these leaderboards on its own.*

**386 models · 18 tokenizer families · 49.5% of the capability matrix verified**

---

## 🎭 The Same Model, Wildly Different Bills

Upstream catalogues list **458 entries** for **386 actual models**. The other
**72** are pricing *modes* — identical weights, different tariff — listed as if they
were separate products. Rank a leaderboard on that feed and you count the same model
three times, at whichever price flatters the chart.

Biggest spread between the cheapest and dearest way to call one model:

| Model | Cheapest | Dearest | Spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | $0.0296 (batch) | $0.15 (standard) | **5.1×** |

## 💸 The Batch Tax

"Batch is 50% off" is folk wisdom, not a rule. **3 models cost *more* in batch
mode than standard** — because the "standard" price is the cheapest routed host while
batch is one specific host's tariff.

| Model | Standard | Batch | Penalty |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | $0.04 | $0.06 | **+50%** |
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | $0.018 | $0.024 | **+33%** |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3` | $0.3794 | $0.45 | **+19%** |

## 🐈 Schrödinger's Cache

Cache economics dominate real agent cost, and the data is a mess. Of 386 models,
**230 publish a cache read price, only 66 publish a cache write price.**

Worse, the ones that publish aren't using the same unit. **222 models** have a
cache price whose billing model is unresolved.

And **19 models report a cache *write* that costs less than a normal read** — an
impossible shape for a one-off write fee. It's almost certainly per-hour storage rent
flattened into the same column as Anthropic-style write premiums. Anyone computing
"cost with caching" from that feed is quietly wrong.

| Model | Input | "Cache write" | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~google/gemini-flash-latest` | $0.75 | $0.041667 | 0.06× |
| `google/gemini-3.6-flash` | $0.75 | $0.041667 | 0.06× |

## 👻 Phantom Tariffs

Prices for things you cannot actually buy. Resellers keep serving a tariff after the
provider has withdrawn the feature.

- `anthropic/claude-opus-4.7` — fast mode was REMOVED on this model - speed:'fast' now errors - yet reseller catalogues still list a priced `-fast` variant. Do not budget against it.

## 🤫 Silent Changes

The errors are survivable. These are worse — same code, different behaviour, no error,
different bill.

- `anthropic/claude-fable-5` — thinking `display` defaults to 'omitted'; on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 it defaulted to 'summarized'. Reasoning is still billed either way.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-4.7` — omitting `thinking` runs WITHOUT thinking. Opus 5 defaults the same request to adaptive thinking.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-4.7` — thinking `display` defaults to 'omitted'; on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 it defaulted to 'summarized'. Reasoning is still billed either way.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8` — omitting `thinking` runs WITHOUT thinking. Opus 5 defaults the same request to adaptive thinking.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8` — thinking `display` defaults to 'omitted'; on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 it defaulted to 'summarized'. Reasoning is still billed either way.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-5` — omitting `thinking` runs adaptive thinking by default. On Opus 4.8/4.7 the same request runs with thinking OFF. Identical code, different behaviour and cost.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-5` — thinking `display` defaults to 'omitted'; on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 it defaulted to 'summarized'. Reasoning is still billed either way.
- `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` — thinking `display` defaults to 'omitted'; on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 it defaulted to 'summarized'. Reasoning is still billed either way.

## 💥 Hard Breaks

Parameters that return an **error** on at least one model. Every one of these is
verified against first-party documentation — the build refuses to ship a `rejected`
claim sourced from a reseller.

| Parameter / feature | Models that reject it |
|---|---|
| `assistant_prefill` | 7 — claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4.6, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-sonnet-5 |
| `fast_mode` | 6 — claude-fable-5, claude-haiku-4.5, claude-opus-4.6, claude-opus-4.7, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-sonnet-5 |
| `temperature` | 5 — claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 |
| `top_p` | 5 — claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 |
| `top_k` | 5 — claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 |
| `thinking_budget_tokens` | 5 — claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 |
| `priority_tier` | 2 — claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 |

## 🗼 Tokenizer Babel

**18 distinct tokenizer families.** A token is a different amount of text in each one,
which is why `$/Mtok` is not a comparable unit and every leaderboard that ranks on it
is ranking on sand.

## 🌑 Deprecation Blackout
